summary: The lecture explains the evolution of money from barter to paper currency, plastic money, and cryptocurrency. It details the Reserve Bank of India's establishment, functions as monetary authority, banker to government and banks, and custodian of foreign reserves. It also outlines the Indian banking structure, scheduled vs non-scheduled banks, priority sector lending via the Lead Bank Scheme, and major development financial institutions.
points: Money defined as generally accepted medium of exchange, payment for goods/services, repayment of debts.
Barter system suffers from double coincidence of wants.
Paper currency standard: currency issued by treasury/central bank, unlimited legal tender.
Plastic money includes cash cards, credit cards, debit cards, prepaid cards.
Cryptocurrency: digital currency using encryption, operates independently of central bank.
RBI established April 1, 1935 under RBI Act 1934; nationalised 1949; headquarters Mumbai.
RBI functions: monetary authority, banker to government (Art. 266,267), banker to banks, lender of last resort, forex custodian, developmental role.
Lead Bank Scheme launched December 1969; priority sectors: small/marginal farmers, artisans, SC/ST, SHGs, minorities.
Scheduled banks maintain reserve requirements with RBI; non-scheduled banks cannot deal in foreign exchange.
Key development institutions: EXIM Bank (1982), NABARD (1982), SIDBI (1990), NHB (1988), MUDRA (2015).
